subject: BridgeKit quick-handoff: SDK quickstart, auth, routing, and local tests
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@clearpark.health>, Chris O'Connell <chris.oconnell@clearpark.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: BridgeKit quick-handoff: SDK quickstart, auth, routing, and local tests

Hi Alex / Chris —

Thanks again for a focused demo earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we have a single source of truth while your engs spin up a local sandbox: 

What we agreed
- Provide a small quickstart repo (Python + TypeScript) that shows auth, basic routing, structured output + a simple tool-calling example, and an embeddings -> reranker flow.
- A local smoke-test checklist so your team can validate latency and model choices before we provision dedicated capacity.
- Short follow-up call to go through your security checklist items (KMS/HSM, VPC requirements).

Immediate action items (owners)
1) We've uploaded a compact bundle: bridgekit_quickstart_overview.pdf and bridgekit_quickstart.zip — contains the two sample apps, README, and a tiny Dockerfile for local validation. (attachment) — Jasmine (sent)
2) Karthik to share a TypeScript auth example showing env var & mTLS fallback patterns, plus a local smoke-test checklist. — Karthik (incoming)
3) ClearPark to confirm required data residency and whether the reranker needs canonicalization for PHI. — Alex / Chris

Quickstart highlights (what to try first)
- Python sample (./python/sample_server.py): shows how to do streaming responses, tool-calling stubs, and structured JSON output parsing.
- TypeScript sample (./ts/bridgekit-client.ts): includes an example embedding call and a simple two-pass reranker.
- Auth: we support API key (env var), short-lived JWT (if you prefer SSO flow), and mutual TLS for private deployments. For ClearPark we recommended API key for initial pilots, mTLS for production.
- Routing: the examples show a simple policy to route low-latency requests to a faster model tier and bulk embedding jobs to a lower-cost pool.

Local sanity checklist (short)
- Node 18+ / Python 3.10+ installed
- set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var or point to local mTLS certs
- run ./local_run.sh, verify /health endpoint, run sample embedding, run reranker sample against the provided mini prompt set (./tests/sample_prompts.json)

Questions for you before next call
- Do you need us to sign an MSA or can we proceed with the standard SOW + data addendum?
- Any specific compliance evidence (SOC2 artifacts) you want attached to the repo?

I'll follow up shortly with the TypeScript auth patch and the checklist. Can we tentatively book 30 minutes on Wed 27 Apr for a short tech review?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

Attachments: bridgekit_quickstart_overview.pdf (PDF, 210KB); bridgekit_quickstart.zip (archive, contains samples)

From: Alex Park <alex.park@clearpark.health>

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 01:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BridgeKit quick-handoff: SDK quickstart, auth, routing, and local tests

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the bundle. A few quick questions after a first pass: 

1) Auth: For production we will require KMS-backed key rotation and support for HSM-backed signing. Can you confirm whether the mTLS option integrates with our internal Cert Authority and whether we can rotate certs without downtime?

2) Embeddings / reranker: what vector dimension and index types are used in the sample? Our reranker needs to run against a vector store with 1024 dims and use approximate nearest neighbor. Will your sample show integration with a local FAISS/Annoy instance?

3) Local testing: one of our devs tried the TS sample on Windows and hit EADDRINUSE on the default port during ./local_run.sh. Any quick suggestions or a port-config option we should set?

4) Also, do you have a short snippet for TypeScript showing how to call the reranker scoring endpoint (we want to replicate the two-pass scoring logic you demoed)?

If you can drop the TS snippet + port-fix guidance into the repo or send here that would unblock us. We are targeting a pilot next month so would like to finalize the security items early this week.

— Alex
Senior Platform Engineer, ClearPark Health
alex.park@clearpark.health
